## Historical audit: S0125

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r2/fixed_h0/H0/test/commons_16007442/trajectory.jsonl`. References below are JSONL lines in this file; the supplied observations contain complete lines, so none requires split-observation offsets.

**Goal versus observation.** The stated goal was to reconstruct a photographed indoor scene with separate meshes and matching camera, framing and materials (student request, line 1). The student’s *interpretation* was an electronics workbench; neither the reference image nor the resulting render is visible in the supplied audit text, so that interpretation and its fidelity cannot be independently checked.

| Stage | Evidence and result |
|---|---|
| Initial build | Student code specified walls, worktop, monitor, instruments, meters, keyboard, cabinets, cables and tools, with colored primitives, a partly transparent lid, poses, camera and lights (student response/execute, lines 3–4). Step 1 timed out after 600 seconds, with no image or diagnostic output (line 5). The cause is unknown. |
| Autonomous revision | After receiving the timeout, the student replaced much repeated SceneAct geometry with material-batched Blender meshes and curves, and reduced intended Cycles samples from 48 to 24 (lines 6, 8–9). Step 2 failed because `sc.world` was `None`; no image resulted (line 10). Batching was an apparent performance response, not proof of the timeout’s cause. |
| Repair and validation | The next program created and assigned a world before configuring it (student response/execute, lines 13–14). Step 3 returned `ok: true`, saved a render and blend file, and was selected (lines 15–16). The render log reports 16 samples despite 24 in the program. This establishes execution success, not visual correctness. |
| Review | The subsequent student request included paths to both reference and rendered images, with zero executions remaining (lines 17–18); the student answered `DONE` (line 19). No explanatory comparison or independent quality assessment is recorded. |

**Scene checks.** Multiple objects and their intended placement are evidenced by the executed program and render log, not by an inspected image. The code gives the monitor and meter grouped parts and rotations, plus wires and a lamp arm; actual contact, alignment, occlusion and pose accuracy remain unverified. It uses colors and roughness, but no image textures are apparent in the final code; whether materials resemble the reference is unknown. Camera and two area lights were explicitly set, but framing and lighting quality cannot be judged. Batching details by material also means not every small object is independently represented as a mesh (line 14).

**Teacher input:** No teacher event, diagnosis, proposed update, or teacher-message receipt appears in this student trajectory. The timeout and traceback were runner feedback, visibly followed by student revisions, not teacher advice (lines 5–6, 10–14).

**Outcome and lessons.** This is a successful final execution after a technical interruption and a code error; reconstruction correctness is **unknown**, not established by `DONE`. Transferably, explicit environment initialization resolved the observed world error, while batching accompanied a later fast successful build. Task-specific choices—object identities, arrangement and camera—remain hypotheses without visual comparison. The precise timeout cause, geometric connections, material fidelity and final image match remain unresolved.
